subject: Blended SLO anchor and monthly credit proposal
messages:
---Message 1---
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@silvertide.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Blended SLO anchor and monthly credit proposal

Asha —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our alignment, attached is a concise proposal for the production SLA anchor and monthly service-credit scheme we think balances Silvertide's availability needs with Redwood's operational guardrails. High-level summary below; see attachments for precise contract language.

Key proposals (summary):
- Availability: 99.95% monthly uptime (global blended) as the baseline guarantee.
- Latency: p95 generation latency target of 450ms measured across primary regions; p95 measured per-region and reported in monthly telemetry.
- Blended SLO: Uptime will be calculated as a traffic-weighted blend across regions (US/EU primary). This allows high-traffic regions to drive the blended % while preserving regional visibility.
- Credit bands (monthly, % of committed monthly bill):
  * >= 99.95%: 0% credit
  * 99.50% — 99.95%: 5% credit
  * 99.00% — 99.49%: 15% credit
  * < 99.00%: 30% credit
- Remedy cap: capped at 1.0x the committed monthly spend for the month of the incident (open to negotiation).
- Carveouts: scheduled maintenance (up to 4 hours/month), customer-caused incidents, force majeure.
- Latency interplay: if p95 exceeds target for more than two consecutive reporting windows and correlates with availability loss, we include a small additive credit (one additional tier).

Attachments: redwood-sla-draft-v2.pdf (contract draft), monthly-credit-matrix.xlsx (detailed examples).

Request: can you confirm if the blended approach and proposed remedy cap are acceptable or whether Silvertide prefers a per-region guarantee with a lower remedy cap? If helpful, Laura and I can jump on a 30-min call with your procurement/legal next week.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
---

---Message 2 (reply)---
From: Asha Patel <asha@silvertide.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@silvertide.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Sep 2026 10:35:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Blended SLO anchor and monthly credit proposal

Jordan —

Thanks for the draft and the clear summary. A few initial questions/concerns from Silvertide's side:

1) Blended SLO: we prefer per-region guarantees for our compliance posture. Blended is OK for reporting, but our procurement/legal will push for explicit per-region minimums (US/EU). Can Redwood provide a floor per-region (e.g., 99.90%)?
2) Remedy cap: 1.0x monthly spend is higher than our standard — can we look at a 0.5x cap instead? We are comfortable with the credit bands but would like an overall cap aligned to our procurement policy.
3) Latency interplay: can you clarify how the additive credit would be calculated and capped? We need something deterministic in the contract.

Cc'ing procurement to surface constraints on remedy caps and to loop in our contracting timeline. We have a procurement window next Wednesday; if we can get a revised doc before then that addresses regional floors and the cap, procurement can proceed with approvals.

Also please confirm whether scheduled maintenance will be announced 7 days in advance and whether there is any blackout for monthly maintenance windows.

Best,
Asha
Head of Platform Engineering, Silvertide Analytics
asha@silvertide.com
---

---Message 3 (internal reply)---
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@silvertide.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Blended SLO anchor and monthly credit proposal

Asha —

Thanks for the fast feedback. I've updated the credit matrix inline below and attached a marked-up draft that reflects our proposed compromise. Key clarifications:

- Per-region floor: we can commit to a 99.90% floor per-region (US/EU) while keeping the blended 99.95% as the global anchor reported in the SLA. The blended metric will appear in the public dashboard but the contract will include per-region floor language.

- Remedy cap: we can accept moving the cap to 0.75x the committed monthly spend (compromise between your 0.5x and our 1.0x). If Silvertide needs 0.5x for procurement policy, we can escalate, but this is our standard compromise.

- Deterministic additive latency credit language: proposed approach in the draft: if p95 latency exceeds the target for two consecutive reporting windows (15-minute windows aggregated to hourly rollups) and that event correlates with an availability bucket that triggers a credit, we add one lower-tier credit (e.g., move from 5% to 15%) but capped at 30% total for the incident month regardless of multiple triggers. This ensures deterministic calc and a clear cap.

- Scheduled maintenance: Redwood will provide >=7 days' notice for non-emergency maintenance; we propose a rolling 4-hour monthly maintenance allowance per region (we call out emergency maintenance separately, which we will always notify as soon as possible).

Revised credit bands (proposal):
- >= 99.95% (blended): 0%
- 99.90% — 99.94% (per-region floor OK): 3%
- 99.50% — 99.89%: 10%
- 99.00% — 99.49%: 25%
- < 99.00%: 45%
Cap: remedy capped at 0.75x monthly committed spend; total credits in a month cannot exceed that cap.

I attached a marked draft (redwood-sla-draft-v2.pdf) and an example workbook (monthly-credit-matrix.xlsx) showing blended vs per-region calculations. Jordan — please let me know if we should nudge the cap lower for this account. Markus — tagging you for any legal redlines on the per-region floor language and the additive latency clause.

Laura Bennett
Senior Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

Cc: Procurement <procurement@silvertide.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Sep 2026 14:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Blended SLO anchor and monthly credit proposal

Laura / Jordan —

Appreciate the clear revisions — this reads much better and the deterministic language helps. We are prepared to move forward on the following points:

- Accept per-region floor of 99.90% and the blended 99.95% anchor for reporting.
- Accept the revised credit bands and the deterministic additive latency clause, with one request: in EU only, due to transit constraints with our regional backbone, can the p95 latency target be 500ms instead of 450ms?
- Remedy cap: procurement will accept 0.75x monthly committed spend.

Procurement will route the contract next week for signature; I'll ask them to include the small EU p95 adjustment in the final SOW. No further blockers from engineering.

Thanks — Jordan/Laura, please send the final marked doc and I'll share with procurement.
